findings.note: Introduced by Senator Gregory (15). Has the state police-standards commission set up a "Missouri Rangers" training program, with fingerprint and criminal-history checks for entrants, to prepare people to respond to violent crises in school settings. A news story says a bill creating the program passed both chambers in May 2026 and went to the governor.

Introduced by Senator Gregory (15). Creates a state income tax credit for parents who enrol a child under 18 in a firearm safety course, including courses that meet concealed carry permit training rules.

findings.passage: The bill’s sponsor, Republican state Sen. David Gregory of Chesterfield, told senators he wanted to give schools “a choice to have a higher trained armed guard.”
findings.note: News story (Muddy River News, from the Missouri Independent) quoting his Senate remarks; only the quoted phrase is his own wording. Explains the aim of the Missouri Rangers bill.

findings.passage: I will always stand strong for our second amendment right to keep and bear arms.
findings.note: His answer on a voter guide profile for the 2022 state auditor race, to the question on what gun ownership restrictions are needed.
